A clear report on Baker's minutes, or the close holding at 23.5+, would have changed it.

Efficiency models put Miami's margin in the high 20s, but buy-game markets sit above those numbers routinely, and the close (-32.5) is near my 31. The most interesting angle is Miami's broken three-point shooting, which limits how fast it can run up a 33-point margin. Against the close the gap is only 1.5, so I pass. A Miami lineup absence or a hot shooting history would have changed it.

The zone-and-pace profile argues for a smaller margin, and the close moved 2 points that way, but Florida's rebounding edge is exactly how teams beat a zone. At the 35.5 close my 33 is a 2.5-point gap, which is too small for early-season NCAAB, where lessons say no edge. A Florida lineup absence would have tipped it.

Illinois's home blowouts and Sam Houston's one-day turnaround point to Illinois, but two rotation players are out (priced) and a short bench eases off in a 30-point game. My 37 is within 2 of the slate and the close, so I pass. The forced side follows Illinois's repeated home margins over the injury storyline.

The sandwich spot (Duke behind, Tennessee ahead) and UNI's real offense point to a smaller margin, and the market already trimmed 2 points from the open. But UNI's defense allows 81 a game, and Michigan State's repeated 30+ wins over buy-game teams match the number. My 25 is only 2.5 under the close, so I pass; the forced side is UNI.

Tennessee's slow, cold-shooting offense and the Michigan State lookahead argue against a 30-point win, and the close already came down to 27.5. But Tennessee's defense and TSU's 30-point loss to Murray State argue the other way. My 26 is 1.5 under the close, a pass.

Prairie View's fast pace, weak defense, fifth game in 11 days and 35-point loss to a lesser SMU team all point to a huge margin, and the market moved 4 points up to 41.5. My 43 sits 1.5 above a number that already absorbed that, so I pass. Walk-on minutes are the main risk to the forced Vanderbilt side.

The slate (-34.5) and close (-30.5) disagree by 4 with no news I could find to explain it, which is a data flag, so I pass. NAU's back-to-back ~30-point road losses and its fatigue point one way; its slow pace, Komin and Kentucky's unconvincing start point the other. Forced side is NAU at the slate number, with my 29 near the close.

The Khamenia injury and both previews' Ohio State picks are priced, and the line still moved to UConn -12.5, so the market sees more than the narrative. Ohio State's 28% three-point shooting against a top-five defense in its first road game points to UConn, but my 12 is within a point of the slate and close, so I pass. Forced UConn rests on the matchup, not the line move.

Duke's bounce-back at Cameron, its 61-point win over Coastal and SIUE's 38-point loss at Missouri point to a huge margin, but the Illinois lookahead, Duke's poor shooting and walk-on minutes cap it. My 45 is within 2.5 of every number, so I pass. Forced side is Duke on the repeated margins.

Virginia's repeated 19+ point wins, including over Arkansas, and Maryland's broken shooting outweigh the fatigue-and-rotation angle for Maryland, but my 7 is only 1.5 past the 5.5 line, so I pass. Maryland resting since Saturday against Virginia's fifth game in ten days is the most interesting angle, and it's the reason I don't go further. A Virginia absence or a short-rotation foul problem would have flipped the forced side.

There's a 3-point slate-vs-close gap with an unexplained late move toward Central Arkansas, which is a data flag, so I pass. Arkansas's rebounding edge and UCA's 32-point loss at Ole Miss point to Arkansas. The Indiana lookahead and UCA's conference-favorite roster point the other way. Forced side is UCA at the slate number, close to my 23.

The models split (KenPom Auburn by 2, Torvik-style Arizona by 3.5) and the line sits between them at Arizona -2.5 after an early move toward Arizona. The most interesting angle is Auburn's shot-blocking against an Arizona offense that can't shoot threes, offset by Auburn's weak defensive rebounding against Arizona's size. Pass. Forced Arizona on the glass edge and the market move.

KenPom (13) sits below the number, but the market moved three points toward Alabama to -18.5 with the Davis-Fleming news already out, and LESSONS says to treat the close as fair. Shading toward the close gives about 18, within 2 of the slate, so pass. The most interesting angle is Seton Hall's defense and rebounding against Alabama's weak defensive glass, offset by a Seton Hall offense that may not keep pace. Forced Alabama: the close moved its way.

Tech's cupcake margins (34 and 18) and poor shooting argue against 39.5, but Stonehill is worse than those opponents and arrives after a travel mess. My Tech-by-35 projection is a soft number, and big college underdogs have been no edge. Pass. The most unusual angle is the ground stop and moved tip. A clean Torvik margin well under 35 would have made Stonehill a lean.

The models (Gonzaga by 7-9), the Wiggins/Almansa news and LSU's untested résumé lean Gonzaga, but money moved the line toward LSU and Gonzaga's hot shooting should cool. My Gonzaga-by-6.5 projection is within about 1 of the 5.5 close. Pass. The surprising angle is Wiggins being cleared two days before the game. LSU's three-point shooting and the reverse movement kept me off Gonzaga.

This is an early-season NCAAB game with conflicting projections: KenPom has it at 5, Covers at 9, and the close at 10.5. My Louisville -9 sits right on the slate number, so I pass. The forced side is Louisville, because of its interior edge against a leaky Memphis defense. The most interesting angle is Louisville losing its first true road game six seasons running. A clear Reid ankle problem or confirmed absences would have changed it.

The only clean projection (9) matches the close (9.5), and there's no unpriced news, so I pass. The forced side is Nebraska: its elite defense against a Boise offense inflated by weak opponents, plus a de facto home crowd in Sioux Falls (the most interesting angle). A Boise shooting outlier is the risk.

Torvik (25.2) and the close (26.5) both sit under the slate's 28.5, but the close already absorbed that, so there's no edge against it and I pass. The forced side is William & Mary, because its offense can score and Michigan can't shoot threes. The most interesting angle is the defending champion's post-May rebuild. A Michigan hot shooting night is what would beat this.

My Texas-by-3.5 matches the close (-3.5), so the slate's +5.5 is a better number than the market's final price, not an edge in itself, and LESSONS says such slate-better sides went 26-37. Pass. The forced side is Baylor: a veteran turnover-forcing defense against a freshman-heavy Texas with an inflated schedule, at a neutral site in San Antonio (the most interesting angle). Confirmed Baylor absences would have flipped it.

KenPom (11) and the close (11.5) are within a point of the slate, so I pass. The forced side is Syracuse: its ball security against a St. John's team built on steals, and a competitive showing against Indiana, while St. John's margins came against sub-196 opponents (the most interesting angle). If Morano plays and St. John's shoots its season 40% from three, it covers.

This is a 46.5-point number on a one-sided mismatch with no real way to beat the close, so I pass. The forced side is USC: UAPB's 364th-ranked offense on a third game in five days, three days after a 69-point loss at UCLA (the most interesting angle), outweighs bench-clearing. A soft Predictem projection (43) is the main counterpoint.

Kentucky's shaky early form and a Torvik projection of about 23 argue for Grambling, but those are public numbers and the close already moved to 28.5. Big college underdogs have been no edge. Pass. The angle is Miranda's foul trouble deciding whether Grambling can stay competitive. A late Kentucky absence would have made Grambling a lean.

LBSU's slow pace, its near-upset at Utah and a Torvik margin around 23 point to the underdog, but UCLA has crushed weak teams by 51 and 69, and the slate and close disagree by 3 points, which lessons treat as a data flag. Pass. The angle is LBSU blowing a 17-point lead at Utah, which shows it can compete. A clean, agreed line near 33 would have made LBSU a lean.

No read. The Giants' better record and defense against a Washington offense missing McLaurin point one way, while Washington's run game against a weak Giants run defense and its heavy blitzing against a leaky Giants line point the other. The close of 1.5 sits right on top of a ~2-3 point projection. The most interesting angle is McCarthy's hip on a short week in wind and rain. A confirmed McCarthy limitation or Winston start would have pushed this to Washington.

Detroit's defense has been much better since Week 5 and New England gives the ball away, but the Lions' offense is scoring under 20 and their secondary is thin with St. Brown questionable. My Lions-by-3 is within a point of the -2.5 close, so no read. A confirmed St. Brown absence or a clean Maye game would tilt it to New England.

The slate (Saints -1.5) and the close (Panthers -1.5) disagree by 3 points, a 4-point swing from the midweek Saints -2.5, which suggests news I could not confirm without risking a leak. Carolina has the better efficiency numbers, but its injury list and Chase Young's pass rush offset that. No read; knowing what moved the line would change it.

Buffalo is better in every efficiency measure and the Jets' offense struggles without Wilson, but the short week, unresolved left-side O-line injuries and the Jets' habit of losing close keep my Bills-by-9 within about a point of the close. No read. A confirmed Wilson absence plus healthy Bills tackles would have pushed me toward Buffalo.

Houston's pass rush against the league's most-sacked QB and Cleveland's penalties point to the Texans, but the Browns are 3-0 at home and win late, and the line hasn't moved off 4.5. My Texans-by-5 is half a point off the number: no read. A confirmed Montgomery return or a Sanders start would have moved it.

Jacksonville is far better on paper and rested, but a 10-10.5 number in a division game against a team that has played several close losses is fair. My Jaguars-by-9.5 is within half a point of the slate. No read. Confirmed absences for Tate and Spears would have nudged it to Jacksonville.

Atlanta's form and its trip back from Madrid point to Kansas City, but Walker is out, Mahomes' elbow was unresolved in my sources, and the line dropped from 4.5 to 3. My own pass trigger is Mahomes' status, which I couldn't confirm, so no pick. A confirmed full-go Mahomes would have made Chiefs at 3.5 a lean at most.

Two bad teams, a rookie QB debut and a 3-point gap between the slate and the close, which LESSONS calls a data flag. The midweek numbers favored Miami, but the close moved away from it and I don't know why. No read. Treating the close as fair, Indianapolis by about 4 covers -2.5, so the forced side is the Colts.

Minnesota's offense has collapsed and Cousins has had only days to learn it, but the Vikings' defense is elite and the market has already moved two points toward Minnesota on the trade. My Packers-by-3 sits on the -2.5 number. No read.

Arizona's offense with a rookie QB and no weapons is dire, but the Rams' passing game is stripped too and the total has dropped to 38.5, so a 9.5-point margin needs a lot. The close has moved to 8.5, and my Rams-by-8 is about a point and a half inside the slate. No read; the forced side takes the points.

Seattle's elite defense against a rookie making his debut is the main factor, but Seattle's offense is 26th in EPA/play with a banged-up Lock, and the trade news is already in the 6.5. My Seahawks-by-7.5 clears the line by only a point. No read.

San Francisco's run game against Dallas's run defense is the clearest mismatch, and the market moved five points to the 49ers. At the slate's 4.5, a point past the 3.5 close, my 49ers-by-3.5 makes Dallas the side, but the gap is only a point. No read.

No read. Pittsburgh's run game against a soft Cincinnati run defense and its bye-week rest are real but known, while the money and the move to a 4.5 close went to Cincinnati. A projection near the close leaves the slate's 3.5 within 1 point. The most interesting angle is Cincinnati's 30-point streak coming against bottom-third defenses, facing an improved Steelers unit. A confirmed absence of both Steelers corners would have pushed it to a Bengals lean.

No read. The Chargers' season-long pattern (0-8, no loss by under 6, last in EPA, sacked constantly) points to Baltimore, but Baltimore is on its fourth QB and has scored 10-13 points in four straight. The close of 3.5 sits about 1 below the slate. A projection of about 5 is within 2 of the 4.5. The most interesting angle is a favorite with two QBs on IR laying points in a 39.5-total game. A Herbert setback in warmups would have made Baltimore a lean.
